key_insight: A tabular foundation model can perform pre-fault dynamic security assessment for many contingencies at once, using in-context learning instead of separate retrained classifiers.
engineering_relevance: This could substantially reduce the labeling, tuning, and maintenance burden for online power-system stability screening while improving generalization to new contingencies.
method: Use a single tabular foundation model for contingency-level stability assessment.
Encode system state features, including electrical distance coordinates (EDC), to support in-context prediction and transfer.
Add a few labeled samples from unseen contingencies when needed to improve generalization without retraining.
evidence_signal: On the IEEE 68-bus system, the model reached about 90% average Macro F1 with only 120 labeled samples per contingency, and 10 labeled samples for a new contingency with EDC matched the best transfer-learning oracle.
watch_item: Generalization to unseen contingencies depends on feature encoding and may still require a small labeled set, so deployment should validate EDC usefulness for the target grid.
paper_title: Revisiting data-driven dynamic security assessment with a tabular foundation model
